📝 NCERT Exercise 1 (Page 159) • Multiple Choice

Which one of the following materials cannot be used to make a lens?

(a) Water
(b) Glass
(c) Plastic
(d) Clay

Correct Option: (d) Clay

Explanation: To make an optical lens, the material must be transparent so that light can easily pass through it and undergo refraction. Water, glass, and transparent plastics are all optical refracting media. In contrast, clay is an opaque material; it absorbs or scatters light and does not transmit light rays at all. Therefore, clay cannot be used to manufacture a lens.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (d) (0.5M) + Reason that clay is opaque (0.5M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 2 (Page 159) • Multiple Choice

The image formed by a concave mirror is observed to be virtual, erect and larger than the object. Where should be the position of the object?

(a) Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
(b) At the centre of curvature
(c) Beyond the centre of curvature
(d) Between the pole of the mirror and its principal focus.

Correct Option: (d) Between the pole of the mirror and its principal focus.

Explanation: For all positions outside the principal focus (at infinity, beyond C, at C, and between C and F), a concave mirror strictly forms real and inverted images in front of the mirror. It is only when the object is brought inside the focal distance — between the pole (P) and principal focus (F) — that the reflected rays diverge in front and appear to meet behind the mirror, forming a virtual, erect, and magnified image.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (d) (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 3 (Page 159) • Multiple Choice

Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real image of the size of the object?

(a) At the principal focus of the lens
(b) At twice the focal length
(c) At infinity
(d) Between the optical centre of the lens and its principal focus.

Correct Option: (b) At twice the focal length (at 2F1)

Explanation: When an object is placed at a distance equal to twice the focal length (u = 2F1 = 2f), a convex lens forms a real and inverted image at twice the focal length on the opposite side (v = 2F2 = 2f). The magnification is m = v / u = +2f / -2f = -1, which means the size of the image is identically equal to the size of the object.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (b) (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 4 (Pages 159–160) • Multiple Choice

A spherical mirror and a thin spherical lens have each a focal length of −15 cm. The mirror and the lens are likely to be:

(a) both concave.
(b) both convex.
(c) the mirror is concave and the lens is convex.
(d) the mirror is convex, but the lens is concave.

Correct Option: (a) both concave.

Explanation: Under the New Cartesian Sign Convention:

  • A concave mirror has its focus in front of the mirror (to the left of Pole), so its focal length is always negative (−).
  • A concave lens has a virtual focus on the incident light side (to the left of Optical Centre), so its focal length is also always negative (−).

Since f = -15 cm is negative for both, both optical devices are concave.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (a) (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 5 (Page 160) • Multiple Choice

No matter how far you stand from a mirror, your image appears erect. The mirror is likely to be:

(a) only plane.
(b) only concave.
(c) only convex.
(d) either plane or convex.

Correct Option: (d) either plane or convex.

Explanation: A flat plane mirror always produces a virtual and erect image of the same size at all distances. A convex mirror also always forms a virtual and erect (diminished) image regardless of the distance of the object. A concave mirror, on the other hand, forms inverted images for all positions outside the focus. Hence, the mirror could be either plane or convex.

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (d) (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 6 (Page 160) • Multiple Choice

Which of the following lenses would you prefer to use while reading small letters found in a dictionary?

(a) A convex lens of focal length 50 cm.
(b) A concave lens of focal length 50 cm.
(c) A convex lens of focal length 5 cm.
(d) A concave lens of focal length 5 cm.

Correct Option: (c) A convex lens of focal length 5 cm.

Explanation: To act as a magnifying glass, we must use a convex lens (concave lenses only diminish images). Furthermore, the magnifying power of a magnifying glass is inversely proportional to its focal length (M ≈ 1 + D/f, where D = 25 cm). Therefore, a convex lens with a shorter focal length (5 cm) yields significantly higher angular magnification and optical power (P = 1/0.05 = +20 D) than a lens of 50 cm focal length (P = +2 D).

📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • Option (c) (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 7 (Page 160) • Conceptual & Ray Diagram

We wish to obtain an erect image of an object, using a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What should be the range of distance of the object from the mirror? What is the nature of the image? Is the image larger or smaller than the object? Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation in this case.

  • 1. Range of Distance: A concave mirror forms an erect image only when the object is placed between the Pole (P) and the Principal Focus (F). Since focal length f = 15 cm, the object must be placed at a distance greater than 0 cm and less than 15 cm from the mirror (0 < u < 15 cm).
  • 2. Nature of Image: The image formed is virtual and erect (formed behind the mirror).
  • 3. Size of Image: The image is larger than the object (magnified / enlarged).
  • 4. Ray Diagram Construction: Draw ray 1 parallel to the principal axis reflecting through focus F; draw ray 2 passing through centre of curvature C reflecting straight back. Extend both diverging reflected rays backwards behind the mirror with dashed lines to intersect at point A'B'.
📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • Range 0 to 15 cm (1M) + Nature & size (1M) + Correct ray diagram with arrows (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 8 (Page 160) • Mirror Applications & Reasons

Name the type of mirror used in the following situations: (a) Headlights of a car, (b) Side/rear-view mirror of a vehicle, (c) Solar furnace. Support your answer with reason.

(a) Headlights of a car — Concave Mirror:

Reason: The high-intensity light bulb is placed exactly at the Principal Focus (F) of the concave reflector. The light rays reflecting from the mirror emerge as a powerful, parallel beam that illuminates the road far ahead.

(b) Side/rear-view mirror of a vehicle — Convex Mirror:

Reason: A convex mirror always produces an erect and diminished image of trailing traffic. Because it curves outwards, it provides a much wider field of view than a plane mirror, helping drivers avoid blind spots.

(c) Solar furnace — Large Concave Mirror:

Reason: Large concave mirrors are converging reflectors. They capture a vast surface area of parallel incident solar radiation and concentrate it onto a small focal point, generating temperatures exceeding 3000°C.

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • 1 Mark for each part (0.5M for mirror type + 0.5M for scientific reason).
📝 NCERT Exercise 9 (Page 160) • Conceptual Verification

One-half of a convex lens is covered with a black paper. Will this lens produce a complete image of the object? Verify your answer experimentally. Explain your observations.

Answer: Yes, the lens will produce a complete image of the object!

Experimental Verification & Setup:

  1. Take a convex lens mounted on an optical stand. Focus the image of a burning candle onto a white cardboard screen.
  2. Cover either the upper half or lower half of the lens with a piece of opaque black paper.
  3. Observe the image on the screen carefully.

Observations & Scientific Explanation:

  • A complete, fully formed image of the candle flame is still observed on the screen at the exact same location with the same size.
  • However, the brightness (intensity) of the image is reduced to half!
  • Why does this happen? Light rays from every point of the object pass through every portion of the lens. The uncovered half still refracts light from all parts of the object to form the entire image. However, because half of the aperture is blocked, only half the original light energy reaches the screen, causing the image to appear dimmer.
📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • 'Yes complete image' (1M) + Explanation that each part forms complete image (1M) + Mention of reduced brightness (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 10 (Page 160) • Convex Lens Numerical & Ray Diagram

An object 5 cm in length is held 25 cm away from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Draw the ray diagram and find the position, size and the nature of the image formed.

1. Given Data with Cartesian Signs:

  • Object height, h = +5.0 cm
  • Object distance, u = -25 cm
  • Focal length of converging lens, f = +10 cm

2. Lens Formula Calculation:
1/v - 1/u = 1/f  ⇒  1/v = 1/f + 1/u
1/v = 1/10 + 1/(-25) = 1/10 - 1/25
LCM of 10 and 25 is 50:
1/v = (5 - 2) / 50 = +3 / 50  ⇒  v = +50 / 3 ≈ +16.67 cm

3. Size of Image (h') and Magnification:
m = h' / h = v / u  ⇒  h' = h × (v / u)
h' = (+5.0) × [ (50/3) / (-25) ] = (+5.0) × (-2/3) = -10/3 ≈ -3.33 cm
m = -3.33 / +5.0 = -0.67

4. Nature & Position Summary:

The image is formed at +16.67 cm on the other side of the lens. The negative signs of v, h', and m show that the image is real, inverted, and diminished (3.33 cm tall).

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • Calculation of v = +16.67 cm (1M) + Height h' = -3.33 cm & nature (1M) + Ray diagram (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 11 (Page 160) • Concave Lens Numerical & Ray Diagram

A concave lens of focal length 15 cm forms an image 10 cm from the lens. How far is the object placed from the lens? Draw the ray diagram.

1. Given Data:

  • Concave lens focal length, f = -15 cm
  • A concave lens always forms a virtual image on the same side as the object: v = -10 cm
  • Object distance, u = ?

2. Lens Formula Calculation:
1/v - 1/u = 1/f  ⇒  1/u = 1/v - 1/f
1/u = 1/(-10) - 1/(-15) = -1/10 + 1/15
LCM of 10 and 15 is 30:
1/u = (-3 + 2) / 30 = -1 / 30  ⇒  u = -30 cm

Answer: The object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of the concave lens.

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • Formula & sign assignment (1M) + Value u = -30 cm (1M) + Ray diagram (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 12 (Page 160) • Convex Mirror Numerical

An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.

1. Given Data:
Focal length of convex mirror, f = +15 cm
Object distance, u = -10 cm

2. Apply Mirror Formula:
1/v + 1/u = 1/f  ⇒  1/v = 1/f - 1/u
1/v = 1/15 - 1/(-10) = 1/15 + 1/10
LCM of 15 and 10 is 30:
1/v = (2 + 3) / 30 = 5 / 30 = 1 / 6  ⇒  v = +6 cm

3. Magnification:
m = -v / u = -(+6) / (-10) = +0.6

Answer: The image is formed at a distance of +6 cm behind the convex mirror. It is virtual, erect, and diminished to 0.6 times the size of the object.

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 Marks • Calculation of v = +6 cm (1M) + Nature (virtual & erect) and magnification (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 13 (Page 160) • Conceptual Meaning

The magnification produced by a plane mirror is +1. What does this mean?

The statement m = +1 has two precise optical implications:

  • 1. The Positive Sign (+) indicates: The image is virtual and erect (upright), formed behind the mirror.
  • 2. The Magnitude (1) indicates: Since m = h' / h = 1, the height of the image is exactly equal to the height of the object (h' = h). Furthermore, m = -v/u = 1 ⇒ v = -u, which means the image distance behind the mirror equals the object distance in front.
📌 Marking Scheme: 1 Mark • 0.5M for virtual and erect + 0.5M for image size equals object size.
📝 NCERT Exercise 14 (Page 160) • Convex Mirror Numerical

An object 5.0 cm in length is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm. Find the position of the image, its nature and size.

1. Given Data:
Object height, h = +5.0 cm
Object distance, u = -20 cm
Radius of curvature, R = +30 cm  ⇒  f = R / 2 = +15 cm

2. Mirror Formula Calculation:
1/v + 1/u = 1/f  ⇒  1/v = 1/f - 1/u
1/v = 1/15 - 1/(-20) = 1/15 + 1/20
LCM of 15 and 20 is 60:
1/v = (4 + 3) / 60 = 7 / 60  ⇒  v = +60 / 7 ≈ +8.57 cm

3. Image Height (h'):
m = h' / h = -v / u  ⇒  h' = - (v / u) × h
h' = - [ (60/7) / (-20) ] × 5.0 = + (3/7) × 5.0 = +15/7 ≈ +2.14 cm

Answer: The image is formed at +8.57 cm behind the mirror. It is virtual, erect, and diminished to a size of 2.14 cm.

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • Focal length f = +15 cm & v = +8.57 cm (1.5M) + Height h' = +2.14 cm & nature (1.5M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 15 (Page 160) • Concave Mirror Numerical

An object of size 7.0 cm is placed at 27 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 18 cm. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed, so that a sharp focussed image can be obtained? Find the size and the nature of the image.

1. Given Data:
Object size, h = +7.0 cm
Object distance, u = -27 cm
Focal length of concave mirror, f = -18 cm

2. Mirror Formula Calculation:
1/v + 1/u = 1/f  ⇒  1/v = 1/f - 1/u
1/v = 1/(-18) - 1/(-27) = -1/18 + 1/27
LCM of 18 and 27 is 54:
1/v = (-3 + 2) / 54 = -1 / 54  ⇒  v = -54 cm

3. Size of Image (h'):
m = h' / h = -v / u  ⇒  h' = - (v / u) × h
h' = - [ (-54) / (-27) ] × (+7.0) = - (2) × 7.0 = -14.0 cm

Answer: The screen should be placed at a distance of 54 cm in front of the mirror (on the same side as the object). The image is real, inverted, and magnified to a height of 14.0 cm.

📌 Marking Scheme: 3 Marks • Screen distance v = -54 cm (1.5M) + Image size h' = -14 cm & nature real/inverted (1.5M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 16 (Page 160) • Lens Power Numerical

Find the focal length of a lens of power −2.0 D. What type of lens is this?

1. Given Data:
Power of lens, P = -2.0 D

2. Formula:
P = 1 / f (in metres)  ⇒  f = 1 / P

3. Calculation:
f = 1 / (-2.0 D) = -0.50 m = -50 cm

Answer: The focal length of the lens is -0.50 m (or -50 cm). Because the focal length and power are negative, this is a diverging lens (concave lens).

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 Marks • Calculation f = -0.5 m (1M) + Identification of concave / diverging lens (1M).
📝 NCERT Exercise 17 (Page 160) • Prescribed Lens Numerical

A doctor has prescribed a corrective lens of power +1.5 D. Find the focal length of the lens. Is the prescribed lens diverging or converging?

1. Given Data:
Power of corrective lens, P = +1.5 D

2. Formula:
P = 1 / f  ⇒  f = 1 / P

3. Calculation:
f = 1 / (+1.5 D) = +10 / 15 = +2 / 3 m ≈ +0.67 m = +66.7 cm

Answer: The focal length of the prescribed lens is +0.67 m (or +66.7 cm). Since the power and focal length are positive (+), the prescribed lens is a converging lens (convex lens).

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 Marks • Calculation of f = +0.67 m (1M) + Identification of converging / convex lens (1M).

SECTION C: Ray Diagram & Multi-step Numerical (2 × 3M = 6 Marks)

11. Draw a neat, labeled ray diagram showing the image formation by a convex lens when an object is placed at twice the focal length (at 2F1). State the three characteristics of the image formed.

Ray Diagram: Ray 1 parallel to axis passes through F2; Ray 2 through optical centre O goes straight. Both intersect exactly at 2F2 on other side. [1.5 Marks]

  • Position: At 2F2 on the other side. [0.5 Mark]
  • Nature: Real and inverted. [0.5 Mark]
  • Size: Equal to the size of the object (m = -1). [0.5 Mark]
📌 Marking Scheme: 1.5M for ray diagram with arrows + 1.5M for three image characteristics.

12. A 4 cm tall object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 20 cm. Calculate the image distance v, magnification m, and the height of the image h'.

1. Given: h = +4 cm, u = -30 cm, f = +20 cm

2. Lens Formula:
1/v - 1/u = 1/f ⇒ 1/v = 1/f + 1/u
1/v = 1/20 + 1/(-30) = 1/20 - 1/30
LCM = 60: 1/v = (3 - 2) / 60 = +1 / 60 ⇒ v = +60 cm [1.5 Marks]

3. Magnification & Height:
m = v / u = (+60) / (-30) = -2 [0.75 Mark]
h' = m × h = (-2) × 4 = -8 cm [0.75 Mark]

Answer: The image is formed at +60 cm on other side. It is real, inverted, and 8 cm tall (two times magnified). [0.5 Mark]

📌 Marking Scheme: Calculation of v = +60 cm (1.5M) + Magnification m = -2 (0.75M) + Height h' = -8 cm (0.75M).

🎯 Exam Practice Zone • High-Yield CBSE Pattern Questions

Practice

Case-Based Study • Dental Examination & Optics

A dentist uses a small handheld mirror to examine a patient's molar tooth located deep inside the mouth. The dentist positions the mirror at a distance of 1.2 cm from the tooth. The mirror produces an erect image that is 2.5 times larger than the tooth.

(i) What type of mirror is being used by the dentist?

(ii) What is the focal length of the mirror?

(iii) Is the image formed real or virtual? Justify.

(i) Mirror Type: Concave mirror (only concave mirror can produce an erect, enlarged image of a real object). [1 Mark]

(ii) Focal Length Calculation:
Given: u = -1.2 cm, m = +2.5 (erect ⇒ positive)
m = -v / u ⇒ 2.5 = -v / (-1.2) ⇒ v = +3.0 cm
Using mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/(+3.0) + 1/(-1.2) = 1/3.0 - 1/1.2 = 1/3.0 - 2.5/3.0 = -1.5 / 3.0 = -1 / 2.0
f = -2.0 cm. [2 Marks]

(iii) Nature: The image is virtual because v = +3.0 cm (behind the mirror) and m > 0; light rays only appear to diverge from behind the reflecting surface. [1 Mark]

📌 Total: 4 Marks • 1M for part (i) + 2M for part (ii) + 1M for part (iii).

HOTS • Lens Immersed in Higher Density Medium

Question: A glass convex lens is immersed in a liquid whose refractive index is greater than that of glass (nliquid > nglass). How will the optical behavior of the lens change? Will it still converge light?

Answer: The optical behavior will reverse completely — the convex lens will behave as a diverging (concave) lens!

Scientific Reason: When nliquid > nglass, the liquid is optically denser than the lens material. When light rays travel from the liquid into the convex lens, they are entering an optically rarer medium, causing them to bend away from the normal (outwards), rather than towards it. Thus, the parallel incoming rays diverge instead of converging!

📌 Marking Scheme: 2 Marks • Reversal to diverging lens (1M) + Explanation of rarer glass causing rays to bend away from normal (1M).
